manifest_changes.heading: Statement
manifest_changes.before: For a compact metric model with unique finite KL minimizer theta*, finite P0 likelihood-ratio means, strictly negative extended relative log contrasts, and finite fractional moments continuous at each alternative, local likelihood-ratio tests combine by a finite cover to give uniformly exponential P0 and Qtheta^n errors on each metric-separated set.
manifest_changes.after:
Assume AC as required by the imported KL and likelihood-density conventions
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]. Let $(\Theta,\rho)$ be a compact metric space in its
metric topology ([[def-metric-compactness]], [[def-metric-space]]). Let
$p_\theta$ be jointly measurable finite-valued probability densities with
respect to one sigma-finite measure $\mu$, and let $P_0$ have supplied density
$p_0$. Suppose $\theta^*$ is the unique minimizer of
$\theta\mapsto\mathrm{KL}(P_0\Vert P_\theta)$ with finite minimum. For every
$\theta$, assume
$$\mathbb E_{P_0}\frac{p_\theta(X)}{p_{\theta^*}(X)}<\infty.$$
For every $\theta_1\ne\theta^*$, assume the extended relative contrast is
well-defined and satisfies
$$\mathbb E_{P_0}\log\frac{p_{\theta_1}(X)}{p_{\theta^*}(X)} =-\left[\mathrm{KL}(P_0\Vert P_{\theta_1})-\mathrm{KL}(P_0\Vert P_{\theta^*})\right]<0,$$
where the value $-\infty$ is allowed. For every such $\theta_1$, assume
that for all $s$ in some interval $(s_0,1)$ with $0\le s_0<1$, the finite
fractional-moment function
$$M_s(\theta_1,\theta):= \mathbb E_{P_0}\left[ \left(\frac{p_\theta(X)}{p_{\theta_1}(X)}\right)^s \cdot \left(\frac{p_\theta(X)}{p_{\theta^*}(X)}\right)^{1-s} \right]$$
is continuous at $\theta_1$. Define its integrand to be zero where
$p_\theta=0$, to be $+\infty$ where $p_\theta>0$ and $p_{\theta_1}=0$, and
to have the displayed value elsewhere; on the $P_0$-null set where
$p_{\theta^*}=0$, assign it value zero. Then, for every $\eta>0$, there are
measurable tests $\phi_n:\mathsf X^n\to[0,1]$ and constants
$c_\eta,C_\eta>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$,
$$P_0^n\phi_n\le C_\eta e^{-c_\eta n},\qquad \sup_{\theta:\rho(\theta,\theta^*)\ge\eta} Q_\theta^n(1-\phi_n)\le C_\eta e^{-c_\eta n}.$$
If the separated set is empty, take $\phi_n=0$. This sufficient
test construction is restricted to the stated compact, unique-minimizer
case; it asserts no generic testability on noncompact parameter spaces.

manifest_changes.heading: Statement
manifest_changes.after:
Use the notation $Pg=\int g\,dP$ from [[def-control-variate-estimator]]. Let $q\ge1$ be fixed and let $(X_i)_{i\ge1}$ be an IID sequence with law $P$. For each $n\ge1$, assume $P|f|^4<\infty$ and $P|h_j|^4<\infty$ for each $j$. Set $\theta=Ph$, define $\Sigma_{jk}=E_P[(h_j-\theta_j)(h_k-\theta_k)]$ and $c_j=E_P[(h_j-\theta_j)(f-Pf)]$, and suppose $\Sigma$ is positive definite, meaning $v^{\mathsf T}\Sigma v>0$ for every nonzero vector $v$. Put $\beta^*=\Sigma^{-1}c$. Define $\bar f_n=n^{-1}\sum_i f(X_i)$, $\bar h_n=n^{-1}\sum_i h(X_i)$,

$$\widehat\Sigma_n=\frac1n\sum_i(h(X_i)-\bar h_n)(h(X_i)-\bar h_n)^{\mathsf T},\qquad \widehat c_n=\frac1n\sum_i(h(X_i)-\bar h_n)(f(X_i)-\bar f_n).$$

and let $\widehat\beta_n=\widehat\Sigma_n^{-1}\widehat c_n$ when $\widehat\Sigma_n$ is invertible and $0$ otherwise. For a scalar random sequence $R_n$, write $R_n=O_P(n^{-1})$ when $nR_n$ is bounded in probability: for each $\varepsilon>0$ some finite $M$ and $N$ satisfy $P(|nR_n|>M)<\varepsilon$ for all $n\ge N$. For a fixed-dimensional vector or matrix, $O_P(a_n)$ means its Euclidean or Frobenius norm divided by $a_n$ is bounded in probability. Then

$$\widehat\mu_{\widehat\beta_n}-\widehat\mu_{\beta^*}=-(\widehat\beta_n-\beta^*)^{\mathsf T}(\bar h_n-\theta)=O_P(n^{-1}).$$

This result bounds only the same-sample coefficient-times-control-mean remainder; it does not assert that $\widehat\mu_{\widehat\beta_n}$ is unbiased.

manifest_changes.heading: Example
manifest_changes.before: For U(q)=q^2/2 and M=1, the exact flow at time pi/2 is (q,p) -> (p,-q). After the required momentum flip the proposal is (q,p) -> (p,q), has zero energy error, and accepts with probability one. Since the refreshed momentum is an independent N(0,1) draw, the returned position is an independent N(0,1) draw.
manifest_changes.after: For the standard-normal target $U(q)=q^2/2$ with $M=1$, exact integration for time $\pi/2$, followed by the required momentum flip, proposes an independent standard-normal position and has acceptance probability one. This is the exact-flow limit; a finite leapfrog map generally has a nonzero energy error.

manifest_changes.after:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be IID $\mathbb R^d$-valued vectors with $\mathbb E\|X_1\|^2<\infty$, mean $\mu$, and covariance $\Sigma$. Fix $a\in\mathbb R^d$ such that $\sigma^2=a^T\Sigma a>0$. For the finite-index empirical bootstrap in [[def-iid-empirical-bootstrap-sample]], let $\bar X_n^*$ be the bootstrap mean and define the conditional CDF
$$F_n^*(x)=\mathbb P^*\!\left(\sqrt n\,a^T(\bar X_n^*-\bar X_n)\le x\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n\right).$$
Then
$$D_n:=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}\left|F_n^*(x)-\Phi_\sigma(x)\right|\longrightarrow0\quad\text{in probability},$$
where $\Phi_\sigma$ is the CDF of $N(0,\sigma^2)$. The assumption $\sigma^2>0$ is needed for the normalized Lindeberg–Feller step.

manifest_changes.heading: Statement refuted
manifest_changes.before: An identifiable finite-data model can have an exact posterior proportional to exp(-n(theta^2-1)^2) on [-2,2]. Both equal global modes have full-rank negative Hessian, yet the one-mode Laplace Gaussian based at +1 stays at least asymptotically 1/2 away in total variation from the full posterior.
manifest_changes.after: A nondegenerate local Hessian at one mode does not by itself ensure that a one-mode Laplace Gaussian approximates the full posterior law in total variation, even when the full-data model identifies the parameter.
